newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MALAYSIA'S ANWAR SAYS JUNE TRADE DEFICIT A CONCERN.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIA'S ANWAR SAYS JUNE TRADE DEFICIT A CONCERN.

text.p: Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Thursday the government was concerned by the sharp rise in Malaysia's June trade deficit to 2.8 billion ringgit.
He told reporters after launching a capital markets conference that import of lumpy items such as ships and aircraft had caused the "temporary" ballooning in the June trade deficit.
"Is this is of some concern, I would say yes. We would have to address them. We will have to take up the issue of reducing imports," Anwar said in a speech referring to the June trade data.
"We have to give all incentives to promote exports," he said.
"When you look at the trade figures, the main import component is lumpy items like aeroplanes and ships. Do you choose to defer these, then MAS (Malaysia Airlines) will not have enough flights.
"These things will temporarily affect the statistics. It will be a temporary factor in the bloating of (the figures)," the deputy prime minister said.
"We need to not necessarily cancel or defer some very important projects. For example, the ports. We cannot defer the expansion of port facilities," Anwar said.
